about.title: Oceanside Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Five people did not come home from Oceanside's roads in 2025. That number sits alongside 835 injury collisions and 1,177 people hurt across the city the same year. Behind each of those five is a San Diego County family working out what comes next. A wrongful death claim is the civil side of that question. It is separate from any criminal case, and it exists so a spouse, domestic partner, or children can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Under California law, close family has the first right to file; certain dependents and heirs may qualify when they do not. Whether the crash happened on Route 76, along Oceanside Boulevard, or at a College Boulevard intersection, the deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, with spouses, domestic partners and children first in line and certain dependents or heirs after that. The attorney you are connected with can sort out where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks considerably when a city, county or state agency is involved. An early connection means those dates are on someone's calendar.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Our service costs nothing, and the independent attorneys in the network handle wrongful death matters on contingency. Your family does not pay legal fees out of pocket while grieving.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on Route 76 near Oceanside. Does a state highway change the deadline?
items.answer: It can. When a government entity such as Caltrans or the City of Oceanside may share responsibility, California requires a formal claim to be presented on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. That is one reason families near these corridors are encouraged to speak with an attorney early rather than waiting on the criminal or insurance process.

items.question: The driver is being prosecuted. Do we have to wait for the criminal case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, independent of what a prosecutor does. Evidence from the criminal case can be useful, but the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of how that case unfolds.

items.question: What losses can our family actually claim?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided over time, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Each category depends on your family's circumstances, so an attorney will walk through them with you rather than offering a number up front.
